newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 12.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 12.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Thursday:
* The Dow climbed 36.56 to close at 7,575.83, surpassing the previous all-time high of 7,539.27, while bonds held steady as traders awaited key U.S. economy reports due on Thursday.

* Indonesia's economy will start recovering this year and achieve sustainable growth in 1998 -- about a year behind most developed countries in the Asia-Pacific region, economist Suhadi Mangusuwondo, a member of the Indonesian National Committee of the Pacific Economic Cooperation Council, said.
* On Wednesday, Jakarta stocks ended higher following modest late buying in selected blue-chips, brokers said. The composite index ended 3.27 points higher at 693.04 points, brokers said.
* On Thursday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,428.00/29.50 at 0150 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,428.50/29.00.

* Blue chip telecommunications firm PT Telkom and PT Indonesia Satellite (Indosat) on a report in the Jakarta Post which quoted the Secretary General of Post, Tourism and Telecommunications Ministry as saying that Indonesia could have 2.4 million cellular phone lines in 1999.
Both state-controlled companies also provide cellular phone services through their subsidiaries.
* Blue chip automobile maker Astra International following an announcement that it expected to post a net profit of 627 billion rupiah (US$258 million) in 1997, up from 470 billion rupiah in 1996.
Astra's finance director Rini Suwandi also said it will launch four new models in 1998 including a compact Asia Family Car which contains 40 percent local component in the first quarter of 1998.
Also on news that Astra's telecommunications subsidiary will participate in the bidding of 11 new cellular licences in Indonesia.

* Semen Cibinong after its shareholders approved a 1996 dividend of 200 rupiah. According to Bisnis Indonesia, the firm has cancelled the construction of the 1.5 million-tonne Tuban cement plant in anticipation of oversupply in 1999.
* Conglomerate Bakrie & Brothers after it failed to win shareholder approval for a bonus share issue plan.
* Polyproplynene producer PT Try Polyta after it posted a net loss of 24.9 billion rupiah in the first quater 1997.
* Bank Tiara after it had received shareholder approval to split the nominal value of its stock from 1,000 rupiah to 500 rupiah and changes in the board of directors and commissioners.

* Retailer Ramayana Lestari as it had revised up its 1997 net profit forecast to 105 billion rupiah against 82.4 billion rupiah in 1996. It had in March revised up its 1997 net profit forecast to 90.2 billion rupiah from the previous forecast of 83.3 billion rupiah.
